Review MeetGeek.ai?

Reviewers mostly see MeetGeek.ai as a dependable meeting recorder and note-taker that saves time with accurate transcripts, strong summaries, easy sharing, search, and useful integrations like Google Calendar, HubSpot, Notion, and major meeting platforms. Several say it beats alternatives on reliability, ease of use, and meeting minutes, and some like features such as sentiment analysis and jumping to exact moments in recordings. The main complaints are inconsistent recording in at least one case, poor support in that case, and gaps like Linux support, speaker or accent recognition, and more flexible recording options.

results.content:
4.8

Based on 26 reviews

Review Tactiq?

Reviewers mostly see Tactiq as a practical way to stop taking manual meeting notes: they praise real-time transcripts, clear summaries, action items, highlights, and the ease of finding past discussion details later. Many say it saves significant time, works smoothly in daily workflows, and handles multiple languages well. A recurring plus is that it feels less intrusive than tools that join calls as participants. The main complaints are inconsistent platform support and quality, especially with Zoom, weak search, patchy Brazilian Portuguese, and missing or limited Microsoft Teams support.

Great meeting assistant, built with collaboration in mind: you can have the transcript and summary, and ask questions about the meeting - super helpful! Works best if the whole company is using it, or at least your department. If you want to just record / transcribe some meetings, there are many other AI notetakers. But if you want to have it across the company, I feel like Fellow is the product to choose, since they are trying to help you organize the whole meeting process: planning before, perform during, and support / store your data securely after the meeting.

Review Fellow.ai?

Reviewers largely see Fellow.ai as a strong, company-wide meeting hub rather than just a recorder: they repeatedly praise accurate transcripts, useful AI summaries and Q&A, shared agendas, action tracking, and the ability to revisit past discussions for alignment, coaching, and follow-up. Many say it works best when adopted across a team or department, helping keep notes, next steps, and context in one place. The main complaints are lighter but consistent: the interface can feel overwhelming at first, some want deeper integrations, and one reviewer says offline mobile use is missing.
